The new m203 10/1 low-amount label established a 4.79-mL onset contrast to its existing high-amount record, weakening the prior expectation of a small cyclic-tertiary-alcohol response. m86's 5/1 onset fell by 5.25 mL across its measured endpoints, while quinoline's 50-to-100-uL onset fell by 3.53 mL and completion rose slightly. These results strengthen endpoint-specific loading questions while motivating stronger-solvent scope checks.

The m72 PE-loading labels did not simply converge to the DCM series: completion was earlier under PE at both amounts, and its amount-response direction differed from DCM. I therefore select matched midpoints to test the interaction directly. The current predictions scarcely distinguish those midpoint protocols.

The previous combined response-shape hypothesis for m80 and m197 must be separated. m80 at 1/1 and 50 uL finished at 7.06 mL, far below the 100-uL completion of 15.66 mL; its neat-EA onset also did not show the predicted increase. The missing high-amount boundary is now more informative than assuming a ratio-wide prolongation. Conversely, m197 finished at 25.00 mL at 2/1 and 26.73 mL in neat EA, rejecting both the predicted intermediate trough and strong-solvent completion decline. I extend that question to related phenolic structures and donor-free controls. The m203 bridge restored ordered endpoints, and m92's 2/1 onset of 6.74 mL weakened its predicted unusually early transition. The previously rejected m92 high-amount completion upturn remains unsupported because identical recorded tuples gave discordant completions.

Pending-CW feedback continued to expose completion errors in ordinary early-eluting rows, including m157 and m140 overpredictions, while other labels were close. The new pending batch supplies substantial coverage of those regions. Historical errors here are acquisition-time errors, not current-model residuals.","batch_rationale":"The pending 16 cover many neutral aromatic conditions, several strong-solvent boundaries and the high-amount primary-alcohol 2/1 condition. These supplements add comparisons that those labels cannot isolate. The paired m72 midpoints complete two amount series and provide a matched protocol contrast. The m51 pair tests whether a demonstrated stronger-solvent loading response disappears at 1/1. Single missing amount endpoints in m86, m19, m107, m13, quinoline and dibenzoylmethane test structural and solvent scope: some may confirm substantial responses, while others may validate nearly flat responses. Their value is learning when each endpoint should change, rather than imposing one loading correction.

The m80 high-amount label resolves a concrete boundary after the latest feedback weakened its broad response-shape interpretation. The m62 bridge tests a current endpoint inversion against measured neighboring ratios. The matched m190 solvent pair addresses completion behavior in a family related to the largest recent failure, while m198 and m191 provide chemically meaningful donor-free boundaries. These complement pending m117 and m186 measurements without duplicating their recorded tuples. Cross-molecule comparisons retain differences in density, sample amount and loading protocol; they do not isolate functional-group causality.

Repeated molecules serve explicit local comparisons, and chemical breadth tests transfer across the supplied Row-distribution. This batch may improve generalization by distinguishing amount effects, protocol associations and endpoint-specific solvent responses in the same model. Quantile spans and CW distances remain diagnostic context, not calibrated epistemic uncertainty or a mandatory ranking rule. Elution interval width is an outcome. These 16 IDs join the pending 16 to freeze all 32 experiments before any new labels; exact packet predictions are retained, with rounding used only in explanatory text."}
